item.content:encoded:
The University of Birmingham is inviting applications for the Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies, an academic opportunity designed to support an early-career researcher whose work focuses on African History and/or African Studies.

Based in the University’s School of History and Cultures in Edgbaston, Birmingham, the fellowship provides an opportunity for an eligible scholar to undertake advanced research, publish academic work, contribute to teaching, and participate in the University’s wider research community.

The position is particularly significant because it is funded through an endowment established to enable academics from sub-Saharan African universities to spend a period of time at the University of Birmingham.

Importantly, this is not an open international postdoctoral fellowship. Applicants must currently be based on the African continent and employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution.

Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies

The successful candidate will join the School of History and Cultures at the University of Birmingham as a Research Fellow in African History.

The fellowship is intended to strengthen the candidate’s research profile while also contributing to the University’s teaching and research activities in African Studies and History.

The role will involve working with a mentor on an agreed programme of research and developing research outputs suitable for publication and academic dissemination.

Key opportunity details

  • Institution: University of Birmingham
  • School: School of History and Cultures
  • Location: Edgbaston, Birmingham, United Kingdom
  • Position: Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies
  • Field: African History and/or African Studies
  • Contract: Full-time, fixed-term
  • Contract period: Up to June 2028
  • Fellowship duration: 18 months
  • Expected start date: 1 January 2027
  • Salary: £36,636–£46,049 per year, with potential progression to £48,822
  • Grade: Grade 7
  • Application deadline: 1 September 2026
  • Job identification: 9655

About the Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship

The Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship is intended to create an opportunity for scholars affiliated with higher education institutions in sub-Saharan Africa to spend a period of research at the University of Birmingham.

During the fellowship, the successful researcher will be able to develop their academic work in an international research environment while contributing to the teaching and intellectual life of the University.

The fellow will work within the School of History and Cultures and will have the opportunity to engage with researchers and students working in related fields.

The fellowship is therefore particularly relevant to researchers who have already completed a PhD in African History or a closely related field and are looking to strengthen their postdoctoral research and publication record.

What will the Research Fellow do?

The successful candidate will have responsibilities across research, publication, teaching, academic engagement and administration.

1. Conduct high-quality research

A central component of the position will be developing and undertaking research within the fellow’s area of historical specialisation.

The fellow will:

  • Develop research objectives and proposals.
  • Conduct research within their area of expertise.
  • Collect and analyse research data.
  • Interpret research findings.
  • Develop new intellectual understandings through their research.
  • Work with a mentor where appropriate.
  • Address challenges that may affect research objectives and deadlines.

Research methods may include literature reviews, interviews, archival or other research approaches appropriate to the field.

2. Develop academic publications

The position places significant emphasis on research outputs and academic publications.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

  • Disseminate research findings.
  • Prepare academic publications.
  • Present research at seminars and other academic events.
  • Prepare papers, posters and other research outputs.
  • Contribute to the University’s research environment.
  • Develop a convincing and achievable research and publication programme.

Applicants therefore need to demonstrate research activity and publications appropriate to their stage of their postdoctoral career.

APPLY HERE.

3. Contribute to teaching

The Research Fellow will also contribute to the delivery of African Studies and History programmes within the School of History and Cultures.

Teaching responsibilities may include:

  • Designing and delivering teaching sessions.
  • Convening undergraduate or postgraduate modules.
  • Delivering lectures.
  • Conducting seminars.
  • Designing and marking assessments.
  • Supervising dissertation students where appropriate.
  • Supporting other teaching-related activities.

Candidates should therefore be able to contribute to teaching at both undergraduate and Master’s level in African Studies and History.

4. Participate in the University’s research community

The successful fellow will contribute to research-related activities within the Department, School and wider University.

This can include:

  • Participating in research seminars.
  • Presenting research findings.
  • Engaging with academic colleagues.
  • Supporting research-related activities.
  • Participating in public engagement activities.
  • Contributing to wider scholarly discussions.

The role therefore goes beyond independent research and encourages the successful candidate to become an active member of the University’s academic community.

5. Support students and other researchers

Depending on the requirements of the discipline and research activities, the fellow may also:

  • Supervise students undertaking research-related work.
  • Provide guidance to PhD students.
  • Support staff or students assisting with research.
  • Offer academic guidance within their area of expertise.

6. Research administration and management

The position may also involve administrative responsibilities arising from the research programme.

The successful candidate may contribute to:

  • Research-related administration.
  • Departmental activities.
  • School-level research activities.
  • Management processes.
  • Public engagement activities.
  • Equality, diversity and inclusion initiatives.

Who can apply?

This fellowship has specific eligibility requirements, particularly concerning the applicant’s location, institutional affiliation and doctoral qualification.

PhD requirement

Applicants must have a PhD focused on the history of Africa and/or African diasporas.

The PhD must have been:

  • Examined and passed between 1 June 2021 and 1 June 2026.

Applicants whose doctoral thesis has only been submitted and is awaiting examination are not eligible.

This means candidates must have successfully completed the examination process within the specified period before applying.

African continent requirement

Applicants must currently be based on the African continent.

In addition, they must be:

  • Employed by an African higher education institution; or
  • Affiliated with an African higher education institution.

This is one of the most important eligibility conditions of the opportunity.

The fellowship is specifically funded to enable members of staff at sub-Saharan African universities to spend a period at the University of Birmingham.

Therefore, applicants living outside Africa are not eligible simply because they are originally from an African country.

The requirement concerns the applicant’s current location and institutional affiliation.

Employment status requirement

Candidates must either:

  1. Not currently hold a permanent academic position, or
  2. If they do hold a permanent academic position, provide a statement with their application confirming that their home institution will release them for the duration of their appointment at the University of Birmingham.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider their employment status before applying.

Other skills and experience required

Successful applicants should be able to demonstrate:

Research experience

Applicants should have evidence of:

  • Active research engagement.
  • Academic publications.
  • Research outputs appropriate to their career stage.
  • Ability to develop independent research.
  • Ability to analyse and interpret research findings.

Research proposal development

Candidates need to demonstrate the ability to develop a convincing and achievable research and publication proposal in African History.

The proposed research should be realistic for the fellowship period and demonstrate clear academic value.

Teaching experience

Applicants should be capable of contributing to:

  • Undergraduate teaching.
  • Master’s-level teaching.
  • African Studies programmes.
  • History programmes.

Administrative and organisational skills

The position also requires an understanding of broader academic management and administrative processes.

Salary and employment conditions

The position is a full-time, fixed-term Grade 7 appointment.

The stated salary range is:

£36,636 to £46,049 per year, with potential progression once in post to £48,822.

The expected start date is 1 January 2027, and the contract is scheduled to run on a fixed-term basis up to June 2028.

The fellowship itself is described as an 18-month postdoctoral fellowship.

Application deadline

The stated closing date is:

1 September 2026

Applicants should ensure that they submit their application before the deadline and allow enough time to prepare their research and publication proposal and demonstrate their eligibility.

Important eligibility point for African scholars

One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that it is not simply a fellowship for anyone interested in African Studies.

The position specifically states that it is limited to applicants who are:

  • Currently based on the African continent; and
  • Employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution.

Applicants must also have a qualifying PhD in the history of Africa and/or African diasporas, completed within the specified period.

Consequently, researchers from African countries who are currently living and working outside Africa may not satisfy the eligibility requirements.

Similarly, an applicant who is currently living in Africa but has no employment or affiliation with an African higher education institution would need to carefully assess whether they meet the stated institutional requirement.

CLICK HERE for more information.

Application considerations

Candidates should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates how they meet the requirements of the fellowship.

A strong application should make it easy for the University to identify:

  1. The applicant’s doctoral qualification.
  2. The date on which the PhD was examined and passed.
  3. Their current location on the African continent.
  4. Their affiliation with an African higher education institution.
  5. Their research specialisation.
  6. Their publication record.
  7. Their proposed research programme.
  8. Their ability to contribute to African Studies and History teaching.
  9. Their ability to participate in the wider academic environment.
  10. Their ability to complete an achievable research and publication programme during the fellowship.

Use of AI in applications

The University of Birmingham specifically provides a warning regarding the use of artificial intelligence in applications.

Applicants are expected to demonstrate their genuine interest in the role and ensure that written application materials accurately reflect their own communication style.

The University states that applications relying too heavily on AI tools may appear generic and may not provide enough detail for the University to properly assess the applicant’s skills.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their application materials are genuinely their own and accurately represent their research experience, academic interests and professional background.

Equality, diversity and inclusion

The University of Birmingham states that it values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive working environment.

The University highlights its work through initiatives and accreditations including:

  • Athena SWAN.
  • Race Equality Charter.
  • Disability Confident accreditation.
  • Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Centre.

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to a fair and equitable workplace and to identify and respond appropriately to equality and diversity issues in accordance with University policies.

Informal enquiries

Applicants who have questions about the position can make informal enquiries to:

Juliet Gilbert

Email: j.gilbert.2@bham.ac.uk

Why this opportunity is significant

The Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship provides an opportunity for an eligible African scholar to spend an extended period conducting research at a major UK university while remaining connected to their academic development and research interests.

For an early-career researcher in African History or African Studies, the position can provide an environment for:

  • Developing new research.
  • Strengthening academic publications.
  • Building international academic connections.
  • Participating in seminars and research activities.
  • Gaining additional teaching experience.
  • Engaging with scholars and students in the UK.
  • Developing a longer-term academic profile.
  • Contributing research on Africa and African diasporas to an international academic environment.

Opportunity Category

Fellowship — Postdoctoral Research Fellowship

Who Qualifies?

This opportunity is specifically aimed at early-career African scholars/researchers who:

  • Have a PhD in the history of Africa and/or African diasporas.
  • Had their PhD examined and passed between 1 June 2021 and 1 June 2026.
  • Are currently based on the African continent.
  • Are employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution.
  • Have evidence of research activity and publications.
  • Can develop a convincing research and publication proposal in African History.
  • Can contribute to undergraduate and Master’s teaching in African Studies and History.

The opportunity is therefore Africa-focused rather than open to applicants from every continent. The current location and African higher education affiliation requirements are particularly important.

Deadline

1 September 2026

Application

Apply for the Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies

item.content:encoded:
Professionals and established researchers working in cultural heritage conservation and preservation have an opportunity to undertake advanced independent research through the Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program 2026.

Organized by the Getty Conservation Institute (GCI), the program provides selected scholars with a three-month residency at the Getty in Los Angeles, California. The residency is designed to give experienced conservation professionals dedicated time and access to specialist resources to develop research projects that can contribute new knowledge, methods, and perspectives to the conservation field.

The program is particularly valuable for professionals whose research can benefit from the Getty’s research collections, library resources, intellectual community, and conservation expertise.

Applications are currently open, and interested applicants must submit their materials by October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7).

About the Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program

The Conservation Guest Scholars Program provides an opportunity for established scholars and professionals who have achieved distinction in the field of cultural heritage conservation to spend three months in residence at the Getty Conservation Institute.

During the residency, scholars are able to pursue their own research projects without their usual work-related obligations. This dedicated research period allows participants to concentrate on projects that could advance professional practice and contribute to wider discussions within cultural heritage conservation.

Scholars also become part of the intellectual community at Getty. During their residency, they can interact with other Getty scholars, fellows, interns, and professionals while making use of resources available at the Getty Center and Getty Villa.

The program has been active since 2000 and remains an important opportunity for professionals seeking to undertake independent research related to the conservation and preservation of cultural heritage.

What Is the Main Goal of the Program?

The central goal of the Conservation Guest Scholars Program is to support research that brings new knowledge and fresh perspectives to cultural heritage conservation.

Getty is interested in projects that can make meaningful contributions to conservation practice. Research may address areas involving cultural heritage objects, collections, architecture, sites, or related conservation and preservation challenges.

Successful applicants are expected to use their residency productively and independently, developing research that has clear relevance to the broader conservation field.

What Does the Three-Month Residency Offer?

Selected Conservation Guest Scholars spend three months in residence at the Getty Conservation Institute.

The available residency periods are:

  • September–December
  • January–March
  • April–June

The grant provides $21,500 for the three-month residency.

In addition to the financial grant, selected scholars receive several forms of practical and research support.

Key benefits include:

  • A $21,500 grant for the three-month residency.
  • A workstation at the Conservation Institute.
  • An apartment in the Getty scholar housing complex.
  • Research assistance.
  • A travel stipend.
  • An available healthcare option.
  • Access to Getty research resources and collections.
  • Opportunities to engage with Getty scholars, fellows, interns, and other members of the intellectual community.
  • Dedicated time to pursue an independent research project without normal work-related obligations.

The terms stated above apply as of August 2026 and may be subject to future changes.

Who Can Apply for the Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program?

The program welcomes applications from researchers and practitioners working in cultural heritage conservation or preservation.

Eligible areas can include work involving:

  • Cultural heritage objects.
  • Museum and heritage collections.
  • Architecture.
  • Historic and cultural sites.
  • Conservation practice.
  • Preservation.
  • Related areas of cultural heritage research.

Applicants must have significant professional experience and an established record demonstrating their contribution to the field.

For more information CLICK HERE.

Professional Experience Requirement

Applicants should have at least seven years of professional experience.

They should also have an established record of:

  • Publications.
  • Professional contributions.
  • Research.
  • Conservation practice.
  • Other achievements demonstrating distinction in the field.

Getty particularly encourages individuals from groups that are underrepresented within the cultural heritage conservation field to apply.

Important Academic Restrictions

The Conservation Guest Scholars Program is intended for established professionals and researchers rather than applicants pursuing initial doctoral-level research.

The program does not consider proposals for postdoctoral research or research that contributes toward a PhD or another academic degree.

Recent PhD graduates in chemistry and other physical or material sciences are instead directed toward Getty’s Postdoctoral Fellowship in Conservation Science, which is a separate opportunity.

Applicants should therefore make sure their proposed project fits the purpose of the Conservation Guest Scholars Program before applying.

APPLY HERE.

Can Applicants Use Getty’s Science Laboratories?

The Getty Conservation Institute may consider proposals that require access to its science laboratories.

However, laboratory use is dependent on:

  • The availability of appropriate laboratory facilities.
  • Staff availability.
  • The amount of available staff time.

Laboratory access therefore cannot be guaranteed.

Applicants whose projects involve Getty’s scientific facilities should also be prepared to conduct their research independently rather than relying on Getty Science department staff to carry out the work.

This is an important consideration when designing the proposed research methodology.

Eligibility for Previous Grant Recipients

Previous recipients of a Conservation Guest Scholar Grant may apply again, but they must observe a six-year waiting period before reapplying.

This means previous participation does not permanently prevent someone from applying again, provided the required waiting period has been completed.

Who Cannot Apply?

Certain individuals are excluded from the program.

The following are not eligible:

  • Current Getty staff members.
  • Members of the immediate families of current Getty staff members.
  • Applicants proposing postdoctoral research.
  • Applicants proposing research that contributes toward a PhD or another academic degree.

Applicants should carefully review these restrictions before investing time in preparing an application.

What Kind of Research Project Is Getty Looking For?

The quality and relevance of the proposed research project are central to the selection process.

A strong proposal should demonstrate an original research topic, a clearly defined methodology, realistic outcomes, and a meaningful contribution to conservation practice.

Applicants should explain not only what they want to research but also why the project matters to the wider field.

A strong project should clearly address:

  1. What is the research problem?
  2. Why is the topic important to cultural heritage conservation?
  3. What methodology will be used?
  4. What part of the research will be conducted during the Getty residency?
  5. What outcomes are expected?
  6. How could the project advance conservation practice?
  7. Why is the applicant qualified to undertake the research?
  8. Why are Getty’s resources particularly valuable to the project?

The strongest applications will make a convincing case that Getty is an appropriate and necessary environment for the proposed research.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit several important components through the Getty Foundation Grant Portal.

1. Project Proposal

The project proposal must not exceed five typed, double-spaced pages.

The proposal must include distinct sections covering:

  • Project description
  • Methodology, including which components will be pursued while the applicant is in residence at Getty
  • Expected outcome
  • Contribution of the project to advancing practice in the conservation field
  • Applicant’s qualifications to execute the project
  • Benefits of Getty resources to the project

Applicants should ensure that the proposal remains focused and clearly connects their research goals with the resources and intellectual environment available at Getty.

2. Abridged Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide an abridged CV highlighting their most relevant professional activities.

The CV must not exceed five typed, single-spaced pages.

Rather than submitting an unnecessarily long professional history, applicants should prioritize experience, research, publications, conservation work, and achievements that demonstrate their ability to successfully complete the proposed project.

3. Selected Bibliography

Applicants must also submit a selected bibliography.

This section should identify scholarly works, other than the applicant’s own publications, that are important to the proposed research and help establish the project’s intellectual framework.

The selected bibliography must not exceed two typed, single-spaced pages.

Applicants should select sources that demonstrate their understanding of the existing scholarship surrounding their research topic.

How Applications Are Submitted

Applications are submitted through the Getty Foundation Grant Portal.

When applications are open, applicants can:

  • Create an account.
  • Update their account information.
  • Create a new application.
  • Save their application.
  • Return later to continue working on the application.

Getty recommends using Google Chrome for the best experience with the application portal. Applicants may also use Firefox or Safari.

Internet Explorer is not compatible with the portal.

Applicants should also be careful when returning to a saved application.

After creating and saving an application form, applicants should return through the “Applications: In Progress” section of the portal. Creating a new application instead of returning to the saved version could result in accidentally creating multiple versions of the same application.

Getty Conservation Guest Scholar Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting application materials is:

October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7).

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Preparing a strong research proposal, CV, bibliography, and supporting materials can take considerable time.

It is advisable to begin preparation well before the deadline and allow sufficient time to review all application materials before submission.

How Will Applications Be Evaluated?

The Conservation Guest Scholar Grants are awarded through a competitive selection process.

Applications are evaluated according to several major criteria.

Overall Quality of the Application

Reviewers consider the strength, clarity, coherence, and overall quality of the submitted application.

Applicants should ensure that all parts of the application work together and clearly communicate the purpose and value of the proposed research.

Contribution to Conservation Practice

The proposed research should have the potential to contribute to the advancement of practice within the cultural heritage conservation field.

Applicants should clearly explain the potential significance of their research beyond their own professional or academic interests.

Applicant’s Past Achievements

Getty considers the applicant’s previous accomplishments and professional record.

A strong history of relevant professional work, publications, research, and other contributions can demonstrate the applicant’s capacity to complete the proposed project.

Qualifications to Undertake the Project

Applicants must demonstrate that they possess the experience, knowledge, and professional expertise required to successfully execute their research.

The proposed project should be realistic in relation to the applicant’s background and capabilities.

Benefit of Getty Resources

Applicants must clearly explain how the project would benefit from Getty’s resources.

This may include:

  • Getty library collections.
  • Research collections.
  • Conservation resources.
  • Getty’s intellectual community.
  • Relevant staff expertise.
  • Other resources available through the Getty Center and Getty Villa.

A strong application should avoid simply stating that Getty is prestigious. Instead, applicants should identify specific resources and explain how those resources will directly support their research.

Letters of Reference Are Not Considered

Applicants should note that letters of reference are not considered in the application evaluation.

Therefore, applicants should focus their preparation on the required application materials and on developing a strong, clearly structured research proposal.

How Does the Selection Process Work?

Applications go through a rigorous screening process involving two separate selection committees.

The committees include:

  • Current Getty staff members.
  • External experts with backgrounds in conservation.
  • Experts from adjacent fields of study outside Getty.

This multidisciplinary review process allows applications to be assessed from both conservation-specific and broader professional perspectives.

What Makes a Strong Application?

According to the program’s evaluation approach, strong applications should demonstrate several important qualities.

Originality

The proposed research should address an original or meaningful topic capable of adding new knowledge or perspectives to conservation.

Clear Methodology

Applicants should explain exactly how they intend to conduct the research and what activities will be undertaken during the residency.

Defined Outcomes

The proposal should identify realistic and meaningful outcomes that could emerge from the research.

Impact on the Field

Applicants should explain how their project could contribute to conservation practice and why the findings could matter to other professionals.

Independent Research Capacity

Applicants should demonstrate that they can work independently, particularly because access to Getty staff expertise and laboratory facilities cannot always be guaranteed.

Strong Case for Getty

One of the most important elements is explaining why Getty is the right place to undertake the proposed research.

Applicants should connect their project directly to Getty’s collections, library, facilities, research environment, or other available resources.

When Will Applicants Receive a Decision?

Applicants are expected to be notified of the Getty Conservation Institute’s decision by March or April 2027.

This means applicants should be prepared for a selection process that continues for several months after the October 2026 application deadline.

Relationship With Other Getty Scholar Programs

The Conservation Guest Scholars Program is related to other Getty residential research opportunities, including the Getty Scholars Program at the Villa.

The Getty Villa Scholars Program supports advanced research that contributes to understanding and preserving cultural heritage, particularly in relation to the arts and cultures of antiquity.

Conservation Guest Scholars and Getty Villa Scholars live within the same complex and participate in shared activities and lectures.

This creates opportunities for intellectual exchange and collaboration between researchers working in related areas.

However, applicants should note that the programs have separate application processes. Applying to one does not constitute an application to the other.

Frequently Asked Questions and Further Information

Getty provides a collection of frequently asked questions addressing common issues concerning its residential grant opportunities.

Applicants who still have questions about the Conservation Guest Scholars Program can contact the Getty Conservation Institute at:

gcischolars@getty.edu

Applicants should use the official Getty information and application portal when preparing and submitting their applications.

Why This Opportunity Is Significant

The Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program can be particularly valuable for experienced cultural heritage professionals who have a research project but lack the dedicated time, facilities, collections, or intellectual environment needed to develop it fully.

The three-month residency creates an opportunity to step away from normal professional obligations and concentrate on an independent research project.

The combination of financial support, housing, travel assistance, research resources, and access to the Getty’s scholarly community makes the program a substantial professional development opportunity.

For professionals working across conservation, museums, heritage sites, architecture, collections, and related areas, the program can provide an environment for developing research with potential implications for the wider field.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Applicants interested in applying can strengthen their submissions by taking a strategic approach.

1. Start With a Focused Research Question

Avoid making the project unnecessarily broad. Clearly identify the problem or question the research intends to address.

2. Explain the Conservation Relevance

Make a direct connection between the research and cultural heritage conservation practice.

3. Make the Getty Connection Specific

Do not simply state that Getty has excellent resources. Identify the particular collections, library resources, facilities, or research environment that will help the project.

4. Demonstrate Independence

Since the research is expected to be independently conducted, applicants should show that they have the expertise and capacity to execute the project.

5. Keep the Proposal Within the Page Limit

The project proposal must not exceed five typed, double-spaced pages. Applicants should therefore prioritize the most important information.

6. Present Relevant Professional Experience

The abridged CV should focus on achievements that demonstrate the applicant’s ability to undertake the proposed research.

7. Develop a Strong Intellectual Framework

The selected bibliography should show that the applicant understands important existing scholarship related to the proposed project.

8. Apply Early

Because the deadline is based on Los Angeles time, applicants in other parts of the world should take the time difference into account and submit before the final deadline.

Key Details at a Glance

  • Program: Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program
  • Organizer: Getty Conservation Institute
  • Location: Getty, Los Angeles, California
  • Residency: Three months
  • Grant: $21,500
  • Housing: Apartment in Getty scholar housing complex
  • Travel: Travel stipend included
  • Work facilities: Workstation at the Conservation Institute
  • Research support: Research assistance included
  • Healthcare: Available healthcare option
  • Professional experience: At least seven years
  • Application proposal: Maximum five typed, double-spaced pages
  • Abridged CV: Maximum five typed, single-spaced pages
  • Selected bibliography: Maximum two typed, single-spaced pages
  • Application deadline: October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7)
  • Decision notification: March or April 2027
  • Application method: Getty Foundation Grant Portal

Conclusion

The Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program 2026 offers established cultural heritage conservation professionals an opportunity to dedicate three months to independent research within the Getty’s internationally recognized research environment.

With a $21,500 grant, accommodation, travel support, a workstation, research assistance, and access to Getty’s collections and intellectual community, the program provides significant support for professionals seeking to develop research that can advance conservation practice.

The opportunity is particularly suited to experienced practitioners and researchers with at least seven years of professional experience and a strong record of publications and other contributions to cultural heritage conservation.

Applicants should focus on developing an original and clearly defined research project, demonstrating a practical methodology, explaining the project’s potential impact, and making a compelling case for why Getty’s resources are essential to the work.

Applications are currently open, and the deadline is October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7). Prospective applicants should carefully review the requirements and begin preparing their proposal, CV, and bibliography well in advance of the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Euro-Mediterranean University (EMUNI) in Koper, Slovenia, is inviting applications for its 2026/27 master’s degree programmes, including two highly relevant programmes for students and professionals interested in international affairs, geopolitics, business, law, technology and global economic transformation.

The two programmes are:

  1. Master’s in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics
  2. Master’s in Business and Digital Law

Both programmes are delivered by EMUNI University in Koper, Slovenia, and provide an international academic environment designed to prepare graduates for careers that increasingly require an understanding of complex global political, economic, legal and technological developments.

The Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics programme focuses on international relations, geopolitics, global power competition, resources, trade, migration, security, diplomacy, regional studies and geoeconomics.

The Business and Digital Law programme focuses on the legal challenges emerging from modern business and digital transformation, including artificial intelligence, data protection, blockchain, cryptocurrencies, financial technology, digital contracts, corporate law and technology regulation.

Both programmes last two years, carry 120 ECTS, are taught in English and begin in October 2026.

1. EMUNI Master’s in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics

The Master’s in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics is an interdisciplinary programme designed for students who want to understand how political power, economics, resources, geography, security, technology and international relations interact across the Mediterranean and the wider world.

The programme is particularly relevant at a time when global power structures are rapidly changing.

Students examine the relationship between states, regional powers, international organisations, businesses and non-state actors, while developing the ability to analyse geopolitical developments and translate complex information into practical policy, diplomatic, business and strategic recommendations.

The programme is directed by Assist. Prof. Luka Juri.

Programme Structure

The programme consists of:

  • 4 semesters
  • 2 academic years
  • 120 ECTS
  • 15 core courses
  • 2 elective courses
  • A master’s thesis

The programme is delivered through full-time blended learning.

According to the programme information, the first semester is online, while the second, third and fourth semesters are conducted on-site.

The study location is Koper, Slovenia.

What Students Learn in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics

The programme combines political science, geography, economics, international relations, regional studies, diplomacy and strategic analysis.

Students explore how:

  • Great powers compete for influence.
  • Regional powers shape political and economic developments.
  • Maritime routes affect international trade.
  • Ports and logistics networks influence strategic decisions.
  • Energy corridors affect regional security.
  • Data cables and digital infrastructure become geopolitical assets.
  • Migration influences political relations.
  • Demographic changes affect economic and political power.
  • Narratives and identities influence conflict and cooperation.
  • Artificial intelligence and cybersecurity are transforming diplomacy.
  • Information warfare is changing international strategy.
  • Natural resources affect geopolitical relationships.

The programme therefore goes beyond traditional political science and provides students with an integrated understanding of political and economic power.

Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics: Learning Outcomes

Graduates are expected to be able to:

  • Analyse regional and global power dynamics.
  • Explain geopolitical developments clearly.
  • Assess risks and opportunities for states, organisations and companies.
  • Analyse Mediterranean and Eurasian geopolitical hotspots.
  • Develop evidence-based policy options.
  • Design strategies and scenarios.
  • Understand international law and governance frameworks.
  • Analyse security, trade, migration and resource-related issues.
  • Communicate and negotiate in sensitive environments.
  • Understand the role of culture, identity and narratives in international relations.

These skills can be applied across government, diplomacy, international organisations, business, consulting, media, research and civil society.

The programme is particularly suitable for people who want to understand how geopolitical and economic developments affect international organisations, governments, companies and societies.

Admission Requirements for Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics

Applicants must generally meet one of the following academic requirements:

  • A completed first-cycle degree equivalent to 180 ECTS or a three-year bachelor’s degree in humanities, excluding languages, or social and behavioural sciences; or
  • A previous higher-education professional study programme meeting the applicable requirements; or
  • A qualification from another professional field equivalent in duration and scope.

Applicants from other professional fields may be required to pass an admission interview covering:

Applicants with qualifications obtained outside Slovenia may be admitted following the applicable foreign-qualification recognition process.

The second programme is the Master’s in Business and Digital Law, an LL.M. designed for students and professionals interested in the legal challenges created by modern business and technological transformation.

  • Law graduates

  • Applicants with equivalent legal qualifications

Applicants from other academic fields may also qualify if they meet the relevant equivalent-degree requirement and complete the prescribed bridge examinations.

Important Advice for Prospective Applicants

Before applying, prospective students should:

  1. Choose the programme carefully. Consider whether your career goals are more closely aligned with geopolitics and international affairs or with business, technology and law.
  2. Check your academic qualification. Make sure your previous degree meets the relevant programme’s requirements.
  3. Check the English requirement. Prepare your B2 certificate if you need one.
  4. Prepare academic documents early. International qualification recognition may require additional time.
  5. Check scholarship availability. Scholarships are limited and competitively awarded.
  6. Prepare a strong application. Highlight relevant academic, professional and research experience.
  7. Apply before the deadline. The current key application deadline is 14 September 2026.
  8. Do not wait for the final period. Later applications may depend on available places.
  9. Consider the financial commitment. Tuition is €5,900 per academic year for each programme.
  10. Think beyond admission. Select the programme based on the career and expertise you want to develop over the next several years.

Conclusion

The EMUNI University Master’s Programmes 2026/27 in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics and Business and Digital Law provide two distinct pathways for students and professionals seeking advanced expertise in areas increasingly important to the global economy and international system.

The Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics programme is ideal for candidates interested in international relations, diplomacy, global power competition, international trade, resources, migration, security, regional studies, policy and strategic analysis. Its interdisciplinary curriculum connects geopolitics with economics, geography, diplomacy, technology and international governance.

The Business and Digital Law programme is designed for candidates interested in the legal side of modern business and technological transformation. Its curriculum covers corporate and commercial law alongside artificial intelligence, European data law, blockchain, cryptocurrencies, financial technology, digital contracts, intellectual property and digital consumer protection.

Both programmes offer:

  • Two years of master’s-level study.
  • 120 ECTS.
  • English-language instruction.
  • A blended-learning format.
  • Study in Koper, Slovenia.
  • International academic exposure.
  • Access to competitive partial scholarship opportunities.
  • Career preparation for internationally relevant professions.

The tuition fee for each programme is €5,900 per academic year.

For the 2026/27 academic year, the current key application deadline is 14 September 2026, while a later application period may be available in September if places remain.

Qualified applicants from Slovenia, other EU countries and non-EU countries can be considered, meaning the programmes can be relevant to prospective students from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, Oceania and other regions, subject to meeting the specific academic and language requirements.

Prospective applicants should review their eligibility carefully, prepare their academic and language documents, investigate available scholarship opportunities and submit their applications as early as possible.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Osaka (UOsaka) accepts international students who receive scholarships from the Japanese Government through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT).

For the 2027 intake, MEXT scholarship opportunities are available at both undergraduate and graduate levels. Applicants can pursue the scholarship through two routes: Embassy Recommendation and University Recommendation.

About the MEXT Scholarship

The MEXT Scholarship is a Japanese Government scholarship programme for international students. At the University of Osaka, MEXT scholarship students can enter undergraduate programmes or pursue graduate-level research leading to master’s or doctoral studies.

At the graduate level, successful applicants usually begin as research students for approximately 6–12 months before proceeding to a master’s or doctoral course after passing the relevant entrance examination.

Study Levels

The opportunity covers:

  • Undergraduate programmes
  • Master’s programmes
  • Doctoral programmes

At undergraduate level, applicants may apply through Embassy Recommendation or University Recommendation. University Recommendation applicants must first pass one of the eligible undergraduate programmes and then be selected as MEXT student candidates.

How to Apply

There are two main application routes:

1. Embassy Recommendation

Applicants are initially recruited and screened by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General in their country.

For graduate applicants, the process includes the embassy’s first screening, followed by the process of obtaining a Letter of Acceptance from a Japanese university and subsequent MEXT and university procedures.

2. University Recommendation

Under the University Recommendation route, the University of Osaka recommends candidates to MEXT. This route is generally connected to universities and research institutions with which the University of Osaka has relevant agreements or collaborative research relationships.

September 1, 2026 Deadline

Applicants who have already passed the first screening by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General and wish to request a Letter of Acceptance from the University of Osaka must apply through the University’s Admissions Assistance Desk (AAD) system.

AAD Application Deadline for AY2027: September 1, 2026, Japan Time.

Applications received from September 2 onward will not be accepted.

It is important to note that this is the AAD Letter of Acceptance deadline, not a general deadline for all MEXT applicants.

Documents Required for the AAD Application

Applicants requesting a Letter of Acceptance through the AAD system must upload the required documents in PDF format, including:

  • Application Form
  • Field of Study and Research Plan
  • Academic transcripts
  • Certificate of graduation or degree
  • Recommendation letter
  • Medical certificate
  • Language proficiency certificate, if available
  • Passing Certificate of the First Screening issued by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General

Additional documents may apply depending on the applicant’s circumstances.

Documents that are not in Japanese or English must be accompanied by a translation into Japanese or English.

Important Information for Applicants

Approval through the AAD system does not itself mean that an applicant has received a Letter of Acceptance from a prospective supervisor.

After receiving the AAD application result, applicants must complete additional procedures, which may include an interview and screening by the prospective supervisor.

Applicants should therefore carefully follow the University’s official instructions and the requirements of their prospective graduate school or programme.

Where to Apply

Applicants who have passed the first embassy screening and need to request a Letter of Acceptance should use the University of Osaka Admissions Assistance Desk (AAD) system.

AAD Application Support System: https://www.ryumon.osaka-u.ac.jp/

Applicants should also consult the official MEXT Scholarship 2027 Application Guidelines and the University of Osaka’s MEXT scholarship information before proceeding.

Conclusion

The 2027 MEXT Scholarship pathway at the University of Osaka provides international students with opportunities to pursue undergraduate and graduate studies in Japan through the Japanese Government’s MEXT scholarship system.

Prospective applicants should first determine which application route applies to them and carefully follow the relevant embassy, university and MEXT procedures. Graduate applicants who have already passed the first embassy screening should pay particular attention to the September 1, 2026 AAD deadline for requesting a Letter of Acceptance.

item.content:encoded:
The Fast Forward 2027 Accelerator is an opportunity for early-stage technology nonprofits using innovative digital solutions to address major social, environmental, health, education, economic, or humanitarian challenges. The programme is designed to help promising tech nonprofits strengthen their organizations, improve their technology and products, access philanthropic capital, develop sustainable growth strategies, and connect with a powerful global community of founders, funders, technology professionals, and social-impact leaders.

Applications for the 2027 cohort open on August 17, 2026, and close on September 7, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (PT).

Fast Forward describes itself as an organization focused on helping entrepreneurs apply the best of technology to some of the world’s biggest social problems. Through its Accelerator and wider ecosystem of resources, the organization brings together the technology, nonprofit, and philanthropic sectors to help technology-driven nonprofits move from early-stage development toward sustainable scale.

According to Fast Forward, it has accelerated 112+ tech nonprofits, which have collectively gone on to impact more than 415 million lives and raise more than $1.4 billion in follow-on funding.

About the Fast Forward 2027 Accelerator

The Fast Forward Accelerator is the organization’s flagship and longest-standing programme for early-stage tech nonprofits.

Rather than functioning simply as a conventional grant programme, the Accelerator combines philanthropic funding, training, mentorship, community, strategic guidance, fundraising support, product development expertise, and visibility.

The programme is specifically designed around the challenges faced by organizations that operate at the intersection of technology and social impact.

Selected organizations receive a combination of:

  • $25,000+ in philanthropic seed capital
  • Tailored training and educational content
  • Mentorship and expert guidance
  • Access to a community of technology nonprofit founders
  • Support with fundraising and nonprofit development
  • Product and technology guidance
  • Growth and scaling strategies
  • Opportunities to connect with funders and supporters
  • Exposure through Fast Forward’s broader ecosystem
  • Participation in Demo Days attended by a large audience of funders and supporters

The programme aims to select approximately 10 teams per cohort, although Fast Forward notes that the exact number can fluctuate depending on the strength and composition of the applicant pool.

What Is a Tech Nonprofit?

A central requirement for this opportunity is that applicants operate as technology nonprofits.

Fast Forward defines a tech nonprofit as a nonprofit organization that uses technology, including artificial intelligence, to address challenges affecting people, communities, society, or humanity more broadly.

Examples can include organizations working in areas such as:

  • Healthcare access
  • Education and education equity
  • Climate action
  • Humanitarian assistance
  • Poverty reduction
  • Digital inclusion
  • Public-interest technology
  • Economic opportunity
  • Community development
  • Social justice
  • Accessibility
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Civic participation
  • Other major social or humanitarian challenges

The defining characteristic is that technology is central to the organization’s solution and social impact model.

Fast Forward points to organizations such as Wikipedia and Khan Academy as examples of technology nonprofits and notes that its directory included more than 1,400 tech nonprofits worldwide as of 2026.

What Support Does the Accelerator Provide?

The Accelerator is structured around three major areas of support: Capital, Content, and Cohort.

1. Capital

Early-stage technology nonprofits often face a difficult funding environment. Traditional nonprofit funders may not understand technology-based business models, while traditional technology investors may not be interested in organizations whose primary objective is social impact rather than financial profit.

Fast Forward seeks to help bridge this gap.

Participants receive $25,000 or more in seed philanthropic capital, while also gaining guidance on navigating the fundraising environment for technology nonprofits.

This funding can provide an important source of early-stage capital as an organization works to strengthen its technology, team, operations, impact measurement, and growth strategy.

2. Content and Training

The Accelerator provides curriculum addressing both sides of the technology nonprofit equation.

On the nonprofit side, participants may receive guidance related to areas such as:

  • Board development
  • Impact measurement
  • Volunteer management
  • Fundraising
  • Organizational development
  • Nonprofit operations

On the technology side, the programme explores topics such as:

  • Product development
  • Go-to-market strategy
  • Technology leadership
  • Scaling
  • Growth
  • Product strategy
  • Sustainable expansion

This combination is particularly relevant to founders who have strong technical or social-impact expertise but need support in strengthening the other side of their organization.

3. Cohort and Community

Building a technology nonprofit can be challenging because founders often face problems that are different from those encountered by traditional nonprofits or conventional technology startups.

The Accelerator therefore places considerable emphasis on peer learning and community.

Selected founders become part of a cohort of organizations facing similar challenges. They also become part of Fast Forward’s broader portfolio and ecosystem, allowing them to build relationships beyond the immediate programme.

This network can provide opportunities for:

  • Peer learning
  • Collaboration
  • Mentorship
  • Knowledge exchange
  • Strategic partnerships
  • Fundraising connections
  • Technology expertise
  • Long-term community support
